prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1031; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The injury does not fit the crash: the impact was very light, yet the claimed injury is severe.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a rear-end collision in which the insured vehicle was struck from behind at a traffic stop. The claimant's representing counsel has asked that all contact go through their office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report, which places the claimant in the vehicle at the scene and records the same sequence of events described in the initial notice.

Entry 3: Spoke with the other driver, who confirmed the stop, the rear impact, and the position of both vehicles as described. Their account matches the photos taken at the scene.

Entry 4: Two witnesses gave statements that agree with the other driver and with each other on the sequence of events. Nothing in their accounts conflicts with the police report.

Entry 5: Inspected the damage to both vehicles. The rear damage on the claimant's vehicle is consistent with the reported impact, though the impact appears to have been light. A few older scratches were noted and may predate this loss.

Entry 6: The claimant's counsel submitted a demand that describes a back injury, with treatment reported as ongoing. The described injury is significantly more severe than the low-speed impact would normally suggest, and this has been noted for review.

Entry 7: Obtained the medical records. The treatment plan followed a usual course for this type of soft tissue complaint, with frequency of visits reducing as the claimant reported improvement. No prior treatment to the same body area appears in the records we have.

Entry 8: Recorded a recorded statement from the claimant through counsel. The account of the collision matches the initial notice in every detail, and the claimant gave the same description in each conversation so far.

Entry 9: Confirmed with underwriting that the driver is named on the policy and that the policy was in force on the date of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the damage occurred before coverage began.

Entry 10: Reviewed the file against the injury claim. The mismatch between the light impact and the severity of the claimed injury remains unresolved, and a medical review has been requested to address it.

Entry 11: Referred the file for an independent medical review and noted that the bodily injury evaluation will remain open until the review is returned and counsel has responded to the questions raised.
